questions.question: The policy of dual system of government of Bengal was the brainchild of which of these?

• The policy was implemented after the** Battle of Plassey in 1757**, which gave the British East India Company control over Bengal, one of the richest provinces in India.
 
• Under the dual system of government, the British East India Company became the** de facto ruler of Bengal, **while the **Nawab of Bengal **remained the** titular head** of the province.
 
• The policy was aimed at ensuring that the British East India Company could **exploit **the resources of Bengal without having to bear the responsibilities of governance.
 
• The dual system of government continued until the **Indian Rebellion of 1857**, after which the British Crown took over the governance of India from the East India Company.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Hastings** was the Governor-General of Bengal from **1813 to 1823**.

 
 
• He is known for his administrative reforms, including the establishment of the** Indian Civil Service **and the introduction of **English education** in India.
 
 
 
• **Lord Lytton** was the Viceroy of India from **1876 to 1880**.
 
 
• He is known for his controversial policies, including the **Vernacular Press Act,** which curbed the freedom of the press in India.
 
 
 
• **Lord Dalhousie** was the Governor-General of India from **1848 to 1856.**
 
 
• He is known for his reforms, including the introduction of the** Doctrine of Lapse, **which allowed the British to annex Indian states that did not have a male heir.

questions.question: What is the duty of the Chief Minister, as mentioned under Article 167 of the Indian Constitution?

options.text: Communication of all decisions of the Council of Ministers to the Governor.
Appointment and removal of Council of the Ministers.
Appointment of the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly.
Appointment of Advocate General of the state in consultation with Attorney general.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**communication of all decisions of the Council of Ministers to the Governor.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 167 **of the Indian Constitution deals with the **duties of the Chief Minister**.
 
• It states that it shall be the duty of the Chief Minister to communicate to the **Governor **of the State all decisions of the **Council of Ministers** relating to the administration of the affairs of the** State and proposals for legislation**. 
 
• This duty is important as it ensures that the Governor is **kept informed** of the decisions taken by the Council of Ministers, who are responsible for the **governance** of the State.
 
• The communication of all decisions of the Council of Ministers to the Governor helps in maintaining** transparency and accountability** in the functioning of the State Government.
 
• It also helps in ensuring that the Governor is able to exercise his/her **constitutional powers and functions** effectively, such as giving assent to** Bills passed** by the State Legislature or **summoning and proroguing** the Legislature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Chief Minister **is responsible for the **selection of the Council of Ministers**, who are collectively responsible to the State Legislature.

 
 
• The Chief Minister can **recommend the removal of a Minister **to the Governor, but the final decision lies with the Governor.
 
 
 
• The **Speaker** is elected by the **members of the Legislative Assembly **from among themselves and is not appointed by the Chief Minister.
 
• The **Advocate General **is appointed by the** Governor **in consultation with the** Chief Minister **and holds office during the pleasure of the Governor.

questions.question: Which of the followings is NOT an example of factor payment?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pension.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Factor payment** refers to payments made to **factors of production,** which are the resources used in the **production of goods and services.**
 
• These factors include **land, labor, capital, and entrepreneurship.**
 
• **Interest, wages, rent,** are all examples of factor payments.
 
• Interest is paid to **capital**, wages are paid to **labor**, rent is paid to** land**, and pension is paid to** retired labor.**
 
• However, pension is **not a** factor payment as it is paid to retired labor and **not to active labor.**
 
• Factor payment is made to the factors of production that are **actively involved** in the production process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Interest** is the payment made for the use of** borrowed capital.**
 
• **Wages** are the payment made to** labor for their services.**
 
• **Rent **is the payment made for the **use of land** and other** natural resources.**
 
• The most widely utilized factor in **macroeconomic analysis** is factor income, which aids governments in identifying the distinction between **GDP and GNP.**
 
• It can also be used to highlight discrepancies in the **allocation of revenue.**

Discount on Original Price = 30%

Profit on Cost Price = 50%

• Option 1,** "The lesson explained the teacher," **is incorrect as it implies the lesson is performing the action, which is illogical.
 
• Option 2, **"The teacher explained the lesson,"** remains in active voice.
